title: Cancer Breakthroughs Update — Jun 7, 2026
summary: ASCO 2026 (May 29–June 2, Chicago) delivered a historically dense set of breakthrough results. The daraxonrasib RASolute 302 Phase 3 trial — received with a standing ovation at the ASCO Plenary and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine — nearly doubled overall survival in metastatic pancreatic cancer (HR 0.40; 13.2 vs. 6.7 months), proving RAS is druggable after 40 years of failure; FDA expanded access is now open. Five-year KEYNOTE-942 data confirmed intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157) sustains a 49% reduction in melanoma recurrence at 5 years (HR 0.51; JCO). Adjuvant selpercatinib (LIBRETTO-432, NEJM) cut recurrence risk by 83% in RET fusion-positive early lung cancer. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (OptiTROP-Lung05, The Lancet) became the first ADC+IO combination to outperform pembrolizumab monotherapy in Phase 3 first-line NSCLC. Ivonescimab became the first China-originated drug ever selected for the ASCO Plenary in 61 years of the organization's history. Post-ASCO, Mayo Clinic's AI model for pancreatic cancer detection up to 3 years pre-diagnosis reinforces the convergence of early detection and targeted therapy in PDAC.

title: Cancer Breakthroughs Update — May 29, 2026
summary: ASCO 2026 opened in Chicago with multiple landmark presentations. The CROWN trial's 7-year lorlatinib update showed approximately 60% of ALK+ NSCLC patients progression-free at 5 years with 92% CNS protection — among the most remarkable outcomes in targeted lung cancer therapy. The HARMONi-6 Phase 3 trial demonstrated ivonescimab, a dual PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, achieves 11.1 vs. 6.9 months PFS over anti-PD-1 alone in squamous NSCLC. Dana-Farber reported 100% MRD-negativity in all 20 patients with high-risk smoldering myeloma treated with CAR-T. On May 28, the NEJM published ASCENT-03 confirming sacituzumab govitecan superiority over chemotherapy in PD-1-ineligible TNBC. The FDA approved Decnupaz (pivekimab sunirine) on May 27 for BPDCN, bringing 2026 oncology approvals to 15+. The daraxonrasib Phase 3 pancreatic cancer plenary is scheduled for May 31.

title: Cancer Breakthroughs Update — May 22, 2026
summary: Two landmark FDA approvals on May 15 reshaped the cancer treatment landscape: Enhertu (T-DXd) became the first antibody-drug conjugate approved for early-stage curative-intent HER2+ breast cancer in both neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings, while atezolizumab (Tecentriq) became the first immunotherapy selected by liquid biopsy, approved for ctDNA-positive muscle-invasive bladder cancer after cystectomy. ASCO 2026 released its full embargo of 7,000+ abstracts on May 21 — the largest in the meeting's history — unveiling Phase 3 data from BREAKWATER (BRAF V600E colorectal), VIKTORIA-1 (PIK3CA breast), and EV-302 (bladder perioperative). Olverembatinib + blinatumomab data from Ascentage Pharma showed 91.3% complete cytogenetic response in relapsed CML at ASCO. The plenary daraxonrasib Phase 3 pancreatic cancer readout is scheduled for May 31.

title: Cancer Breakthroughs Update — May 15, 2026
summary: The FDA approved sonrotoclax (Beqalzi) on May 13 as the first BCL-2 inhibitor specifically targeting relapsed/refractory mantle cell lymphoma after BTK inhibitor failure, with 52% overall response rate and 15.8-month median duration of response in 103 patients — addressing a critical unmet need in BTK-resistant MCL. On May 8, Bizengri (zenocutuzumab) received accelerated approval for NRG1 fusion-positive bile duct cancer, extending the bispecific HER2/HER3 antibody's pan-tumor reach to three NRG1+ cancer types. The FDA also granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to emiltatug ledadotin (ADC) for adenoid cystic carcinoma on May 12 — one of the most promising early targeted therapy candidates for this rare, incurable salivary gland malignancy. Additionally, the liquid biopsy field's resolution section has been updated to reflect the February 2026 NHS-Galleri trial miss (primary endpoint not met), adding context for the ongoing debate over MCED screening readiness. ASCO 2026 full abstracts release on May 21, with daraxonrasib's Phase 3 plenary on May 31.

title: Cancer Breakthroughs Update — May 07, 2026
summary: The world's first PROTAC protein degrader drug, Veppanu (vepdegestrant), received FDA approval on May 1 for ESR1-mutant ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer — inaugurating a new therapeutic class that destroys the estrogen receptor rather than blocking it. The FDA simultaneously authorized expanded access for daraxonrasib in pancreatic cancer following Phase 3 data showing 13.2 vs. 6.7 months median OS. Daraxonrasib's Phase 1/2 results were published in NEJM on May 6 (30% response rate at 300 mg). Additional developments include a JACR study showing AI mammography triage captures 50% of screen-detected cancers in the top 2% of scans, and a Mount Sinai Cell Reports Medicine paper demonstrating that quad-target immunotherapy (PD-1+CTLA-4+LAG-3+TREM2) overcomes checkpoint resistance in treatment-refractory colorectal cancer.
